testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: Verify branch is rebased on base (needs pull-request context and full git history, not the worktree); Validate renovate.json (fetches renovate from the npm registry via npx on every run); smoke-omp (needs bun and a globally installed pinned omp binary); install-and-smoke (needs bun and a globally installed pinned omp binary).

refuted.claim: When the install read fails, `route` dispatches a Cell the install does not run, with REASON=ok and UNRUNNABLE=-. That is the silent level clamp this PR exists to prevent, and the ledger line cannot tell 'not checked' from 'checked, nothing unrunnable'. The only signal is a stderr WARNING, and the exit stays 0.
refuted.evidence: Probe: catalog where every model runs only low/medium, then route. Readable install: `POLICY=slow-medium CELL=slow-low DRAW=1/1 BY=every-5th ... UNRUNNABLE=slow-high,slow-max,...,task-xhigh REASON=table-cell-unrunnable`. Same table with --catalog pointing at a missing file: `POLICY=slow-high CELL=slow-high DRAW=- BY=- ... UNRUNNABLE=- REASON=ok`, status 0, stderr `WARNING cannot read what this install runs: ENOENT ... — no Cell is checked against it`. The existing test 'an install it cannot read warns...' asserts UNRUNNABLE is `-` for this case.
refuted.suggested_fix: Make the unread state visible in the Routing line, for example UNRUNNABLE=? or a REASON such as `install-unread`, so the ledger and cockpit can show the Pull was dispatched unchecked. If a spare token is too invasive, fail the Pull when the read fails and the table names a Cell.

votes.reason:
The behaviour the claim describes is real, but it is intended and not silent. I read plugin/scripts/ticket-router.mjs (the route command's install read) and tests/ticket-router.test.mjs in the snapshot. I did not run the suite or the probe, so there is no red or green run.

- When `readInstall` returns null, the code calls `warn('cannot read what this install runs: ... - no Cell is checked against it and no exploration Cell is drawn')`. It then routes with `install` null.
- A code comment in the same block states the design: a read that fails or does not answer in OMP_READ_TIMEOUT_MS leaves the Pull's Cells unchecked and its every-5th draw empty, and 'warns, never the exit'.
- Several tests assert this, including 'route: an omp that does not answer is killed and warns, the Pull still routes, exit 0', and a missing-files case for a burn-in Pull and a chain head. The test the claim cites, 'an install it cannot read warns...', asserts UNRUNNABLE is '-' for this case.
- The claim reports a stderr WARNING and exit 0. That matches the stated design and does not show a silent level clamp.
- The suggestion that the ledger line cannot tell 'not checked' from 'checked, nothing unrunnable' is a design preference. It is not a defect in the merged code.

refuted.claim: A failed install read in `metrics-refresh` silently reopens an already-ended burn-in and persists it. Only stderr warns; the `fit:` stdout line and `router-fit.json` carry no sign that the read failed. An install that runs no level at all is not even warned about here, although `ticket-router route` warns for it.
refuted.evidence: Fixture with smol on a no-level model, run 1: stderr empty, `burn_in:false, starting_cells:[slow-high,task-high]`. Run 2, same corpus with --catalog missing: exit 0, stderr WARNING, stdout `fit: fitted 40 Pulls, in burn-in; ...`, router-fit.json now `burn_in:true, starting_cells:[slow-high,task-high,smol-high]`. Run 3, model-roles `{}`: exit 0, stderr `""`, again burn_in:true with all three Cells. A single 10s omp timeout in close-out therefore moves the router from every-5th exploration back to burn-in draws.
refuted.suggested_fix: Carry the failed read into the Fit or the `fit:` stdout line, e.g. `fit: ... (install unread: counting all three starting Cells)`. Alternatively keep the previous Fit's starting_cells when the read fails. Emit the same 'runs at no level' warning that ticket-router emits.

votes.reason: Not run; I read the code at the snapshot's metrics-refresh.mjs:386-397 and ticket-router.mjs:430 and 1106. A failed install read does warn on stderr ("WARNING cannot read what this install runs ... burn-in counts all three starting Cells"), so the 'silent' part is overstated. Falling back to all three starting Cells is documented as intended in the startingCellsOf doc: 'so that an install that cannot run them is no reason to end burn-in'. A no-level install returning all three Cells without a warning is real in the code, but it is the same designed fallback. I found no defect beyond what the PR documents. unverified.claim: rowDispatch's `adjust` swaps a tripped or unrunnable row Cell for the derived default (defaultCellOf) without checking whether that default is itself tripped. When slow lacks `high` and the guard has tripped `slow-medium`, the Pull is dispatched to the tripped `slow-medium` with REASON=table-cell-unrunnable.
unverified.evidence: probes/p1.mjs: installOf with slow thinking [low,medium,xhigh] and the shipped agents dir, then rowDispatch({table: burn_in false, rows *=slow-high, guard:{tripped:['slow-medium']}, objective:'cost', stratum:'*'}) printed `P1 default slow-medium` and `{"policy":"slow-medium","reason":"table-cell-unrunnable","draw":{...}}`. Before this PR the fallback was always POLICY_CELL, the guard's baseline, which pr-cost.mjs:250 never trips (`t.cell === BASELINE_CELL` is skipped). Reach is narrow: phase 0 refuses any install where slow lacks high, because 3 non-implementer definitions use @slow:high (counted with grep/awk over copy/plugin/agents). So this only happens if the install changes mid-run.
unverified.suggested_fix: Make defaultCellOf skip tripped levels (pass guard.tripped in), or document that a tripped derived default is still dispatched.

unverified.claim: With no cost guard and an install whose slow model lacks `high`, the cockpit's dispatch heading says every Pull runs at slow-high. The same tab's root row shows slow-medium and labels slow-high 'held: no cost guard' rather than unrunnable. The tab therefore disagrees with route, which the ticket says it must not.
unverified.evidence: A temporary test in copy/tests reused the fixtures from compute-cell-evidence.test.mjs:1-575 and called policy({ guard:{status:'missing'}, catalog: opus-5 thinking [low,medium,xhigh,max] }). It printed `PROBE {"heading":"no cost guard: every Pull runs at slow-high, the default Cell","cell":"slow-medium","held":"slow-high held: no cost guard"}`. dispatchHeading(table, guard) is not given the install and hard-codes POLICY_CELL. Same narrow reach as the first finding.
unverified.suggested_fix: Pass inst.install into dispatchHeading and word it with defaultCellOf(install). In rowEntry, check unrunnability before the guard-missing wording.

unverified.claim: A Routing with REASON=table-cell-unrunnable and UNRUNNABLE=- is possible because rowDispatch tests ladders only while unrunnableCells lists only defined Cells. The board card then renders `cost row's Cell (one of ) unrunnable here: default Cell`.
unverified.evidence: probes/p1.mjs P2 called route() with an install that has no definitions and a task ladder without xhigh, against rows *=task-xhigh. It printed `POLICY=slow-high CELL=slow-high ... TRIPPED=- UNRUNNABLE=- REASON=table-cell-unrunnable`. probes/p3.mjs passed that line to cellLine({row:'#5 impl-5', issue:5, routed:[...]}) and got `["slow-high","cost row's Cell (one of ) unrunnable here: default Cell"]`. It is reachable only when a row names a Cell that has no definition, or when the agents dir is empty (route already warns about the latter).
unverified.suggested_fix: In reasonWords, when r.unrunnable is empty and rowCell is undefined, fall back to `${row}'s Cell unrunnable here`. Alternatively, have rowDispatch's unrunnable test agree with unrunnableCells.

unverified.claim: With the install unreadable, behaviour matches the ticket. Run against the ticket's smoke fixture, the readable case shows the every-5th draw re-centred on the default Cell, with task-max (next task level above high on a ladder without xhigh) among the candidates.
unverified.evidence: probes/smoke.mjs ran the CLI with a Fit whose * rows are task-xhigh, task thinking [low,medium,high,max], smol thinking null, impl-row 5. It exited 0 with `POLICY=slow-high CELL=task-max DRAW=3/3 BY=every-5th ... UNRUNNABLE=smol-high,smol-low,smol-max,smol-medium,smol-xhigh,task-xhigh REASON=table-cell-unrunnable` and a WARNING that smol runs at no level. Pointing --catalog at a missing file also exited 0, printing `POLICY=task-xhigh CELL=task-xhigh DRAW=- ... UNRUNNABLE=- REASON=ok` and the 'cannot read what this install runs' WARNING. This is a confirmation, not a defect.
unverified.suggested_fix: None needed.

unverified.claim: Removing `routable` weakens the tier-check gate. A role whose model runs some levels but none that any defined implementer Cell uses now passes with a notice only, although the router then still dispatches the unrunnable default Cell.
unverified.evidence: checkRoutes with only fleet-implementer-slow-high defined and every role on a model whose catalog thinking is [low, medium]: violations [] and notices include `cell slow-high unrunnable: modelRoles.slow → p/m runs low, medium`. `defaultCellOf` on the same install returns `slow-high` (POLICY_CELL), so route dispatches it with only a stderr warning. The old code made POLICY_CELL always routable, so this was a violation.
unverified.suggested_fix: Keep the violation when no Cell of the policy role is both runnable and defined, not only when slow runs at no level: the condition in main's `defaultCellOf(install) === POLICY_CELL` warning.

unverified.claim: A Fit whose `starting_cells` is malformed (a string, an empty list, or unknown Cell names) is accepted by validateTable. The cockpit falls back to all three starting Cells with no signal, so burn-in progress is judged over a different set than the one that set `burn_in`.
unverified.evidence: validateTable on the starting table with starting_cells 'x', [], ['nope'] and undefined returns valid for every one. The test at compute-cell-evidence.test.mjs:996 asserts that `['nope']` gives 3 cells. countedStartingCells has no flag or heading for the substitution.
unverified.suggested_fix: Validate `starting_cells` in validateTable, or have the cockpit say the recorded set is unusable.

unverified.claim: readInstall's try covers installOf and readdirSync as well as the reads. A bug or an odd modelRoles value thrown from installOf or resolveRole is reported as 'cannot read what this install runs: <message>' and treated as an unread install.
unverified.evidence: Read only: the catch returns `{ install: null, why: e.message }` for every exception in the block. A probe with number or object role values did not throw: models became null, so every Cell was unrunnable and starting Cells fell back to all three silently. No installOf throw was triggered.
unverified.suggested_fix: Wrap only the three reads. Let installOf failures surface as themselves, or label them differently.

unverified.claim: countedStartingCells' validation of a recorded `starting_cells` is only partly tested: dropping the `recorded.length > 0` check, changing `.every` to `.some`, and returning `[...recorded]` instead of `STARTING_CELLS.filter(...)` (which loses canonical order) each leave all tests green.
unverified.evidence: Mutants (a) `recorded.length > 0 && recorded.every` -> `recorded.every`, (b) `recorded.every((c) => STARTING_CELLS` -> `recorded.some((c) => STARTING_CELLS`, (c) `STARTING_CELLS.filter((c) => recorded.includes(c))` -> `[...recorded]`. Each run: node --test over the 8 files above → exit 0, fail 0 (survived). Baseline same command → exit 0, tests 644 pass 644. The existing test at compute-cell-evidence.test.mjs:996 only passes `["nope"]`, so no case has an empty array, a mix of valid and invalid cells, or a reordered set.
unverified.suggested_fix: Add cases to the compute-cell-evidence test: `starting_cells: []` → all three; `["slow-high","bogus"]` → all three; `["task-high","slow-high"]` → canonical order slow-high, task-high.

unverified.claim: The `parsed === null` guard in isRunnable is untested: removing it leaves every test green. It is unreachable for valid Cells, so it is probably an equivalent mutant.
unverified.evidence: Mutant `install === null || parsed === null ||` -> `install === null ||` → node --test over the 8 files → exit 0, fail 0. Baseline exit 0, 644/644.
unverified.suggested_fix: Either add a test of isRunnable with a non-Cell string, or drop the dead guard.

unverified.claim: No discrimination gap found in the rest of the diff: the other 28 mutants were each caught by a test whose name matches the changed behaviour.

The per-test baseline is the whole-set green, not a separate green for each named test.

unverified.claim: Untouched doc step 3 says `tier-roles.mjs --check` validates that each definition's level is one its role's target runs at, with no qualification, but this diff makes that a notice (not a violation) for implementer definitions unless `slow` runs at no level.
unverified.evidence: docs/components/tier-routing.md:29-33 in the snapshot reads 'validates ... that each definition's level is one the role's target runs at (omp's model catalog)'; tier-roles.mjs:305 now pushes `cell ... unrunnable: ...` to notices for implementer definitions and only violates for `slow` with no levels.
unverified.suggested_fix: Add 'except an implementer definition, which the router routes around and --check reports as a notice' to that step.

unverified.claim: The new `starting_cells` field on the Fit table is recorded but never checked by validateTable. Nothing stops a non-empty, STARTING_CELLS-only set from being the only thing that holds. A non-array or empty value passes validation, and only compute-cell-evidence re-checks it at read time.
unverified.evidence: `grep -n starting_cells plugin/scripts/*.mjs` finds only the writer (ticket-router.mjs:980), the cockpit reader (compute-cell-evidence.mjs:539, which defensively re-validates with Array.isArray / length>0 / every in STARTING_CELLS) and comments. validateTable's checks (lines ~322-324) cover `cells` and not `starting_cells`. The invariant is held by the producer plus a defensive reader, not by validateTable.
unverified.suggested_fix: Validate `starting_cells` in validateTable as an optional, non-empty, duplicate-free subset of STARTING_CELLS. The cockpit could then drop its own re-check.

unverified.claim: fitTable, fitTree and writeFit accept any `startingCells` array. An empty array makes `shortStartingCells` empty and so sets `burn_in` false immediately. The non-empty invariant lives only in startingCellsOf's fallback, not at the Fit entry points.
unverified.evidence: The diff shows `startingCells = STARTING_CELLS` as an unvalidated default parameter in fitTable, fitTree and writeFit. `shortStartingCells = (n, cells) => cells.map(...).filter(...)` has no empty check. startingCellsOf returns `runs.length > 0 ? runs : [...STARTING_CELLS]`, which is the only place non-emptiness is enforced.
unverified.suggested_fix: Throw in tableOver (or fitTable) when startingCells is empty or holds a Cell outside STARTING_CELLS.

unverified.claim: `isRunnable(install, cell)` treats a cell that does not match CELL as runnable (`parsed === null`). A malformed Cell therefore passes the install check instead of being rejected. `install.ladders[parsed[1]]` also assumes the parsed role is a key of `ladders`. That is true only because CELL's role alternation (slow|task|smol) and ROLES_BY_PRICE (smol, task, slow) are kept in sync by hand.
unverified.evidence: The diff body of isRunnable is `install === null || parsed === null || install.ladders[parsed[1]].includes(parsed[2])`. ledger-grammar.mjs:993 defines CELL as /^(slow|task|smol)-.../ and ticket-router.mjs:393 defines ROLES_BY_PRICE separately. validateTable ensures table cells match CELL, so this is unreachable for table rows today.
unverified.suggested_fix: Derive ROLES_BY_PRICE or the ladders keys from the same source as CELL, or assert at module load that they match. Throw on a non-CELL string instead of answering true.

unverified.claim: The Routing UNRUNNABLE field is documented as 'sorted', but parseRouting and formatRouting only check that each item matches CELL. Unsorted or duplicated lists parse and round-trip, so the stated invariant is documented and not enforced. The same goes for `unrunnable` and `tripped` being disjoint from nothing.
unverified.evidence: The diff line `unrunnable: unrunnable.every((c) => CELL.test(c)) ? unrunnable : undefined` is the only check. The header comment says 'lists every Cell ... sorted'. formatRouting's round-trip via parseRouting does not compare order. unrunnableCells does sort at the producer.
unverified.suggested_fix: Either drop 'sorted' from the grammar doc, or reject unsorted and duplicate lists in parseRouting, as is done for other fields.

unverified.claim: rowDispatch's `install = null` conflates 'install not read' with 'no install information', so 'nothing is unrunnable' is a runtime convention and not something the types force. The three-valued shape, install-or-null plus a `why` string, is split across readInstall's return and the caller. A caller can pass `install` without handling the null warning path.
unverified.evidence: readInstall returns `{ install, why }` where the two are meant to be mutually exclusive (`{install, why:null}` or `{install:null, why}`), but it is a plain object with no tagged union. compute-cell-evidence's installFrom builds a parallel `{ install, why, note }` shape by hand.
unverified.suggested_fix: Optional: return a tagged result (e.g. `{ ok: true, install }` | `{ ok: false, why }`) so the two cannot be inconsistent.

unverified.claim: parseRouting's legacy-line padding uses an if/else-if with an off-by-one splice (`UNRUNNABLE_AT - 1`) for the two-short case; two sequential single-purpose pads, PARENT first, give the same result with no index arithmetic.
unverified.evidence: Replaced lines 1092-1097 in simplify/copy with the two-line form below, then ran simplify/probe-routing.mjs, which compares snapshot parseRouting against copy parseRouting over 390 lines (the full 13-key line with every combination of 0-3 words dropped, plus each adjacent-word swap): `{ lines: 390, parsedSame: 3, diff: 0 }` (the 3 that parse: full, minus UNRUNNABLE, minus PARENT+UNRUNNABLE). `node --test` over ledger-grammar, compute-cell-evidence, ticket-router, metrics-refresh, compute-board-cell-line, board-cell-evidence-gather, tier-roles, cockpit-tabs and member-bodies-split test files in the copy: tests 659, pass 659, fail 0.
unverified.suggested_fix:
if (words.length === ROUTING_KEYS.length - 2) words.splice(PARENT_AT, 0, "PARENT=-");
if (words.length === ROUTING_KEYS.length - 1) words.splice(UNRUNNABLE_AT, 0, "UNRUNNABLE=-");

unverified.claim: modelChanges takes `inst` only to forward it to countedStartingCells, which reads `inst` only when `p === null`, and modelChanges has already returned [] for `p === null`. So the parameter (and the fitView argument) does nothing.
unverified.evidence: In the copy I changed the signature to `modelChanges(p)`, passed `null` to countedStartingCells at line 550, and changed fitView to call `modelChanges(p)`. The 659-test run passes, including the notices assertions in compute-cell-evidence.test.mjs. From the code: countedStartingCells' only `inst` use is `if (p === null) return startingCellsOf(inst.install)` (snapshot line 538).
